pr_title: Allow `py3x-none` tags in newer than Python 3.x
pr_body:
Unlike `cp36-...`, which requires exactly CPython 3.6, `py36-none` is compatible with all versions starting at Python 3.6.

Note that `py3x-none` should not be used. Instead, use `py3-none` with `requires-python`. 

Fixes #7800

comments: For whatever reason, [`solace-pubsubplus`](https://pypi.org/project/solace-pubsubplus/#files) only publishes wheels for Python 3.6, and you're using Python 3.11.9. So it's correct to fail here: the project has no source distribution (so you can't build it), nor does it have built distributions for the Python version you're on.
That’s interesting! Solace-pubsubplus works in Poetry on Python 3.11.9. Poetry seems to handle the package differently, and I thought this might help us understand why UV fails to resolve it.
How does Poetry behave? Does it allow you to _install_ the package, or just resolve it to the lockfile?

review_comments: Does this entire part make sense? In the example above, I thought cp36 was a lower-bound, so it _would_ match`==3.10.*`.

`cpxx-<...>-<...>` as a python tag only really makes sense in combination with a matching ABI tag, `cp311-none` doesn't really make sense: why are you requiring CPython if you're not requiring its ABI? For pragmatic reasons, we're following pip (on python 3.12), `cp` is an exact python tag unless we use `abi3`, then it's a minimum version, while `py` is a lower bound:


What if the version is greater than our own upper-bound on Python? E.g., `py310` but the user has `== 3.8.*`.
I guess we don't handle this at all here yet (upper bounds).
